1812.describe_en: Low-power immunohistochemical stain of a bone marrow core biopsy shows diffuse, strong membranous staining in sheets of cells that fill the intertrabecular marrow spaces, with only rare negative cells and scant residual fat. The pattern of involvement is diffuse rather than nodular or paratrabecular. The antibody is not labeled on the image; in the context of this case, the staining most likely represents a pan-B-cell marker such as CD20 or PAX5. Findings are consistent with extensive marrow involvement by diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

ddx.vs: B-cell infiltrates are characteristically paratrabecular and CD10/BCL2-positive with small cleaved cells, rather than diffuse large cells.
Can be diffuse CD20-positive but cells are small, CD5/CD23/LEF1-positive with weak CD20.
Diffuse PAX5/CD79a-positive infiltrate but cells are TdT and often CD34 positive with dim or absent CD20.
Diffuse infiltrate is CD138-positive and CD20-negative in most cases.

60308.recognize_zh: 視野中許多紅血球比中央小淋巴球的核還小、染色深且缺乏中央淡染區（central pallor），呈圓球狀，並夾雜略帶藍灰的多染性紅血球，符合遺傳性球形紅血球症的球形紅血球（spherocytes）。
features: Numerous small, round, densely staining red cells lacking central pallor (spherocytes)
Spherocytes are smaller than the nucleus of the adjacent small lymphocyte
Scattered larger bluish polychromatophilic red cells indicating reticulocytosis
Admixed normal discocytes with central pallor, producing a dimorphic appearance
Occasional crenated red cells, likely preparation artifact
60308.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a mixed population of red cells with numerous spherocytes, which are small, round and hyperchromatic without central pallor and measure less than the diameter of the small lymphocyte nucleus in the center of the field. Scattered polychromatophilic cells are present. Some crenated cells are seen, likely artifactual. No schistocytes, agglutination or bite cells are identified. Findings are consistent with spherocytosis; in the appropriate clinical and family context (negative DAT, increased osmotic fragility or reduced EMA binding), this supports hereditary spherocytosis.

ddx.vs: Spherocytes look identical, so a positive direct antiglobulin test rather than morphology distinguishes immune hemolysis from hereditary spherocytosis.
MAHA shows schistocytes (helmet and triangular fragments) and thrombocytopenia, whereas this smear shows round intact spherocytes without fragments.
HPP shows marked microspherocytes together with bizarre fragments, budding forms and elliptocytes, which are not present here.
In thick areas all red cells lose central pallor uniformly, whereas true spherocytes coexist with normal discocytes in a thin, well-spread area as here.

148.recognize_zh: EDTA 血液抹片中，多顆小血小板一圈圈貼附在嗜中性球的細胞膜外緣，形成玫瑰花環（rosette），而其他地方游離血小板很少，這就是血小板衛星現象（platelet satellitism），會造成假性血小板低下。
features: Multiple platelets adherent in a ring around the plasma membrane of segmented neutrophils (rosetting)
Involved neutrophils are otherwise normal: 3-5 lobes, condensed chromatin, fine granules, no toxic change
Neutrophils with satellitism tend to aggregate into small clusters of two to five cells
Adherent platelets are normal-sized and granular; free platelets in the background are relatively sparse
Background red cells normocytic with mild crenation and refractile drying artifact; no platelet-only clumps
148.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear prepared from an EDTA-anticoagulated sample shows clusters of segmented neutrophils surrounded by rings of adherent platelets, forming distinct rosettes. The neutrophils themselves show normal nuclear segmentation and granulation, and the adherent platelets are of normal size and granularity. Free platelets are relatively sparse in the background, and the red cells show only mild crenation and drying artifact. Findings are consistent with EDTA-dependent platelet satellitism, an in vitro phenomenon that can cause spurious thrombocytopenia; repeat count on a citrated or heparinized sample is recommended.

ddx.vs: Clumping shows free-floating aggregates of platelets not attached to leukocytes, whereas satellitism shows platelets rimming neutrophils.
True thrombocytopenia shows uniformly few platelets without rosettes or clumps and persists in citrate-anticoagulated samples.

ddx.dx: Neutrophil phagocytosis of platelets (in vivo, e.g., ITP or sepsis)
ddx.vs: Phagocytosed platelets lie within the neutrophil cytoplasm, often in vacuoles, rather than adhering to the outer cell membrane.
Toxic granules are intracytoplasmic azurophilic granules, whereas satellite platelets sit outside the cell border and have their own pale hyalomere.

captions: Low power: a cluster of three neutrophils rimmed by adherent platelets amid sparse free platelets.
Two neutrophils; the left one is encircled by a dense rosette of platelets.
Two adjacent neutrophils with platelets adherent around their membranes.
Cluster of five neutrophils with prominent platelet satellitism (out-of-focus debris at left).

84.recognize_zh: 真皮內片狀排列、胞質豐富淡嗜酸性的細胞，核呈卵圓形並有明顯核溝、摺疊（coffee-bean／腎形），外觀像 Langerhans 細胞；S100 強陽性、CD1a 樣膜染色部分陽性，但 langerin 陰性，指向 indeterminate dendritic cell tumor。
features: Diffuse sheets of large mononuclear cells with abundant pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and indistinct cell borders
Oval to reniform nuclei with prominent longitudinal grooves and nuclear folds, fine chromatin and small nucleoli (Langerhans-like)
Aggregate of small mature lymphocytes at the edge; eosinophils are not prominent
Strong diffuse nuclear and cytoplasmic S100 positivity in lesional cells
Partial membranous/cytoplasmic staining for a second dendritic-cell marker (likely CD1a; label not provided)
Lesional cells negative for a third marker (consistent with langerin), with only rare background positivity
84.describe_en: Skin biopsy shows a diffuse dermal infiltrate composed of sheets of large histiocytoid cells with abundant pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, admixed with a small aggregate of mature lymphocytes. The lesional cells have oval to kidney-shaped nuclei with conspicuous nuclear grooves and folds, fine chromatin and small nucleoli; significant eosinophil infiltration, necrosis or marked pleomorphism is not seen. By immunohistochemistry (markers not labeled on the images), the cells are strongly positive for S100, show membranous staining for a dendritic-cell marker consistent with CD1a, and are negative for a marker consistent with langerin. Findings are consistent with indeterminate dendritic cell tumor; absence of Birbeck granules by electron microscopy supports the diagnosis.

ddx.vs: LCH cells have identical grooved nuclei and are S100+/CD1a+ but are langerin (CD207)-positive with Birbeck granules and usually have admixed eosinophils, whereas these cells are langerin-negative.
RDD histiocytes are S100+ but CD1a-negative, have round nuclei with prominent nucleoli and show emperipolesis, not grooved Langerhans-like nuclei.
JXG shows foamy histiocytes and Touton giant cells that are CD68/CD163/factor XIIIa-positive and CD1a-negative, usually S100-negative.
IDCS is S100+ but CD1a- and langerin-negative, typically nodal with spindled/fascicular growth.

84.stain: H&E; IHC (S100, likely CD1a and langerin; labels not shown)
captions: H&E: sheets of histiocytoid cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm; small lymphocyte aggregate at top right
High power H&E: grooved, folded Langerhans-like nuclei with abundant pale cytoplasm
IHC (likely CD1a): partial membranous/cytoplasmic staining in lesional cells
IHC S100: strong diffuse nuclear and cytoplasmic staining

20.recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片可見單葉或核分離的小型發育不良巨核細胞（dysplastic megakaryocytes），切片以脂肪為主呈低細胞性；核型圖只有一條第 7 號染色體（箭頭），FISH 也呈 7 號單倍體訊號，在兒童合併疣與淋巴水腫時要想到 GATA2 缺乏症（Emberger syndrome）。
features: Aspirate: dysplastic megakaryocytes including a hypolobated/monolobated form and a small megakaryocyte with two widely separated round nuclei
Cluster of megakaryocytes with hypolobated, eccentric nuclei within a particle (image slightly out of focus)
Core biopsy: hypocellular marrow with predominance of adipocytes and scattered small hematopoietic islands
Karyotype: single chromosome 7 (arrow) indicating monosomy 7 in a male karyogram
Interphase FISH with D7S486 (7q31)/CEP7 probes showing a single-copy signal pattern consistent with monosomy 7
20.describe_en: The bone marrow aspirate shows dysmegakaryopoiesis, with small hypolobated/monolobated megakaryocytes and megakaryocytes with separated round nuclei; blasts are not increased in the fields shown. The core biopsy is hypocellular for age, composed predominantly of adipose tissue with scattered small hematopoietic islands. The G-banded karyogram shows loss of one chromosome 7 (arrow), and interphase FISH with the D7S486/CEP7 probe set shows a single-signal pattern supportive of monosomy 7, although signals are small at this magnification. In a child with warts and lymphedema, findings are consistent with hypocellular myelodysplastic syndrome with monosomy 7 arising in germline GATA2 deficiency (Emberger syndrome).

ddx.vs: Also hypocellular, but lacks dysplastic megakaryocytes and clonal cytogenetic abnormalities such as monosomy 7.
Morphology may be identical, so germline GATA2 sequencing and the clinical triad of warts, lymphedema and monocytopenia/B/NK lymphopenia separate the syndromic form.
Also a germline predisposition with childhood monosomy 7 and hypocellular marrow, distinguished only by germline genetic testing and associated clinical features.
Hypocellular marrow with dysplasia in children, but characterized by chromosome breakage on DEB/MMC testing and congenital anomalies rather than GATA2 mutation.

captions: Aspirate: dysplastic megakaryocytes, monolobated (left) and with separated nuclei (right)
Aspirate: cluster of hypolobated megakaryocytes within a particle
Core biopsy: hypocellular marrow with predominance of fat
Interphase FISH D7S486/CEP7: single-copy signal pattern consistent with monosomy 7

2388.recognize_zh: 骨髓切片中央有一片中型、核圓至卵圓、染色質細緻淡染、細胞質少且邊界不清的細胞群聚，其中可見核分裂，周圍仍殘存正常顆粒球與嗜酸性前驅細胞；此圖未見菊花團（rosette）或神經纖維網，形態本身無法與母細胞區分，需靠免疫染色確認為轉移性神經母細胞瘤。
features: Central cluster/sheet of intermediate-sized cells with round to oval nuclei and finely dispersed, pale chromatin
Scant, poorly defined cytoplasm with syncytial appearance
Mitotic figures within the tumor cell aggregate
Residual normal hematopoiesis at the periphery, including granulocytic and eosinophilic precursors
No Homer Wright rosettes or fibrillary neuropil identified in this field
2388.describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy (H&E) shows a central aggregate of intermediate-sized cells with round to oval nuclei, finely dispersed pale chromatin, and scant ill-defined cytoplasm, with mitotic figures, surrounded by residual granulocytic and eosinophilic hematopoiesis. Homer Wright rosettes and fibrillary neuropil are not identified, so on morphology alone the infiltrate cannot be distinguished from a hematolymphoid blast population. Immunohistochemistry (PHOX2B, synaptophysin, chromogranin, with negative CD45/TdT) and urine catecholamines are required. With that support, the infiltrate is compatible with metastatic neuroblastoma.

ddx.vs: Blasts infiltrate diffusely rather than in cohesive syncytial nests and are CD45, TdT, CD34, or MPO positive, while neuroblastoma is PHOX2B and synaptophysin positive.
Shows membranous CD99 and nuclear NKX2.2 with EWSR1 rearrangement and is PHOX2B negative.
Shows myogenin/desmin positivity and FOXO1 rearrangement.
Consist of maturing mixed-lineage cells without cohesive nests, mitotically active syncytial clusters, or neuroendocrine markers.

3988.recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的中性球體積偏大，核分成 6 葉以上（≥6 葉即為過度分葉），背景可見多種髓系前驅細胞與胞質深藍、染色質較疏鬆的大型紅系前驅細胞；過度分葉中性球是巨母細胞性貧血（megaloblastic anemia）的重要線索。
features: Arrowed neutrophil with six or more nuclear lobes (hypersegmentation), slightly enlarged
Other large granulocytic forms with band-like or ring-shaped nuclei, suggestive of giant bands/metamyelocytes
Large erythroid precursor (upper right) with deep blue cytoplasm and open, finely granular chromatin, suggesting megaloblastic change
Mixed myeloid precursors including promyelocytes/myelocytes
Red cells with anisopoikilocytosis, including teardrop and fragmented forms
3988.describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cellular mixture of granulocytic and erythroid precursors. The arrowed neutrophil is enlarged and hypersegmented with at least six nuclear lobes, and additional large granulocytes with band-like or ring-shaped nuclei suggest giant bands or metamyelocytes. A large erythroid precursor with deeply basophilic cytoplasm and open, finely stippled chromatin is also present, and red cells show anisopoikilocytosis. Findings are consistent with megaloblastic hematopoiesis, as seen in vitamin B12 or folate deficiency; serum B12, folate, methylmalonic acid and homocysteine should be correlated.

ddx.vs: MDS can show megaloblastoid erythroid change but typically has hypogranular or pseudo-Pelger neutrophils rather than hypersegmentation, with normal B12/folate levels.
Drug effect is morphologically identical and is distinguished only by medication history with normal vitamin levels.
The rare benign hereditary form shows hypersegmented neutrophils without macrocytosis, giant metamyelocytes or megaloblastic erythroid precursors.

1620.recognize_zh: 這是 Giemsa 染色的薄切片（塑膠包埋型），滿視野中大型淋巴樣細胞，核呈泡狀、可見小核仁，夾雜少數小淋巴球與胞質淡染的巨噬細胞，符合反應性淋巴組織（生發中心）中轉化細胞為主的區域。
features: Predominance of medium to large lymphoid cells with round to oval vesicular nuclei
Fine to open chromatin with one or more small, distinct nucleoli
Scant to moderate pale blue cytoplasm; cell borders visible in the thin section
Admixed small lymphocytes with dense dark nuclei, concentrated at the upper right
Scattered macrophages with abundant pale cytoplasm and occasional apoptotic debris
Heterogeneous (polymorphous) population rather than a monotonous sheet
1620.describe_en: Giemsa-stained thin section of lymphoid tissue shows a cellular field composed predominantly of medium to large transformed lymphoid cells with vesicular chromatin and small nucleoli, admixed with small mature lymphocytes and scattered pale macrophages containing debris. The population is heterogeneous, with a mixture of cell sizes and no monotonous sheet of atypical cells. Architecture cannot be fully assessed at this magnification. Findings are consistent with a reactive germinal center-rich area of normal lymphoid tissue.

ddx.vs: DLBCL forms sheets of monotonous large cells effacing architecture, whereas this field retains a mixed population of small lymphocytes, transformed cells, and tingible-body-type macrophages.
Burkitt shows uniform medium-sized cells with a very high mitotic rate and a diffuse starry-sky pattern, not the variable cell sizes seen here.
Neoplastic follicles lack polarization and tingible-body macrophages and are BCL2-positive, which requires architecture and immunostains beyond this field.
